כָּלָה rendered as light verb plus complement, thou mayest make an end, headed on end (rule 44); the of by which the English verb reaches its bare object belongs to this rendering (rule 44's supplied-preposition clause), and the determiner an joins the complement under rule 15.

מֵעַל is a contiguous compound preposition rendered by the single word against, so the two morphemes fuse under rule 30. Headed on the governing מִן, as the same מֵעַל → from at NUM.17.5 and both מֵאֵת → of pairs at NUM.17.2 are: neither morpheme carries a lexeme the other lacks, so the syntactic head decides and the ASV's choice of English preposition does not move a source head (rules 23, 24). Heading on עַל, whose sense against carries, was the competing reading, and marking one of the two unrepresented was the other.
Suffix to me.
The waw of the result clause takes the subordinator that written for it (rules 14, 55).
Negative to not; discontinuous from the verb it negates under rule 25.
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on die.

review_notes: Both clause-initial waws are rendered by that and take it under rules 14 and 55.
make an end of is read as a light verb with its complement and the supplied object preposition (rule 44).

Reconciliation: the fused מֵעַל was re-headed from עַל onto the governing מִן, to match NUM.17.5's מֵעַל and NUM.17.2's two מֵאֵת pairs. The English against is a target-side fact under rule 24 and does not choose the source head; the competing reading is named in that unit's note.
